- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 3–5 days at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish signals, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends; if true price drops >3% from recent high, adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment is mixed or declining, reduce forecast volatility by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows no clear trend, model tends to forecast mean-reversion bias; use 3–5 day moving average of recent prices as baseline.
